Small/dense groups include increases: largest mean percentage is mixed64 interpreter +182272bytes/+2.346percent, positive in both rounds (+208896/+155648bytes); array64 JIT is +124928bytes/+1.632percent. These are retained as observed tradeoffs, not dismissed as noise. Retained-snapshot cases preserve their necessary copies and have mixed signs; largest mean increase is array interpreter +571392bytes/+1.069percent, with +1089536/+53248byte observations. The unequal observations do not establish a stable regression or its cause. Remaining positive means are all smaller. Accept this bounded implementation with these explicit local peak-memory limits because all semantics pass, allocation totals/slopes do not regress in the covered matrices, and large no-snapshot memory improves consistently in every runtime/payload group. This does not certify leak freedom, retained heap, universal memory neutrality, production sizes or clean-host speed. Broader representation review remains open.
